newsitem.title: UK: PROFILE - List of Billiton's operations.
newsitem.headline: PROFILE - List of Billiton's operations.

text.p: Base metals group Billiton Plc effectively demerged from South Africa's Gencor Ltd as conditional trading in its shares began on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
The following is a list of the main activities of Billiton, which was bought by Gencor from Royal Dutch/Shell Group for $1.2 billion in 1994:
-- Billiton has seven divisions: aluminium; titanium minerals; steel, ferroalloys and nickel; coal; base metals; marketing and trading and new business and exploration.

-- Aluminium is the most profitable division. It made up 40 percent of the 189 million pound ($316.3 million) attributable profit stemming from production operations in the nine months to March 31, 1997.
The aluminium operations are among the world's biggest and are based in Australia, Brazil, South Africa and Surinam.
-- Titanium minerals made up 24 percent of profits.
It consists of a 50 percent interest in South African-based RBM. Anglo-Australian Rio Tinto holds the remainder.
-- Steel, ferroalloys and nickel made up 13 percent of profits.
Billiton has a 52.55 percent stake in Johannesburg-listed Samancor Ltd and a 98.88 percent interest in Colombia-based in CMSA.
Billiton intends to merge its nickel operations with Australia's QNI Ltd, which would create the fourth biggest producer of the metal in the world.
Billiton would hold at least 55 percent in any new entity.
Billiton has a 42.3 percent interest in South Africa's Ingwe Coal Corp Ltd, which is the country's largest coal producer.
-- The base metals division, which focuses on other base metals than aluminium and zinc, made up five percent of profits.
It has a zinc and copper operation in Quebec, Canada as well as a zinc mining business in the North West province of South Africa.
-- Marketing and trading generated a nine-month attributable profit of seven million pounds.
-- New business and exploration posted a 46 million pound loss over the nine month period to March 31.
